content: AWS official guidance says transactional outbox stores the business change and event in one database transaction, then publishes committed rows asynchronously. At-least-once delivery can duplicate events, so consumers must be idempotent and ordering should be explicit. PostgreSQL documentation confirms SKIP LOCKED is appropriate for multiple consumers of queue-like tables, not general reads. For Oblivious this supports a shared PostgreSQL outbox and lease-based worker substrate before any service extraction.
